precepts.text: God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. And Adam begat a son in his own likeness, after his image, and called his name Seth. Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone's not made in God's image. Cain was not made in God's image; Seth was; Abel was. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he wasn't God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.
precepts.point: The earth also was corrupt before God: because the sons of God started to mingle with the daughters of men, Cain's children. Cain gained dominion on the earth. And the earth was filled with violence: just like Cain was violent. Is the earth full of violence today? Yes. The end of all flesh is come before me; behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Who are the men here? Eve said of Cain that she had gotten a man from the Lord, so the daughters of men are Cain's children. The sons of God came out of Adam's line through Seth. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain's daughters.

Genesis 5 shows why Seth's line is called the sons of God: “In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.” God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.”

Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone is not made in God's image. Seth was, and Abel was, but Cain was not. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he was not God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.

So when the sons of God, made in God's likeness through Seth, took the daughters of Cain, the line that was in God's image mixed with the line that was not. The children “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown”: powerful, famous, fierce fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain. Cain had built a city, and the sons of God began dwelling in it and following his ways, just as the sons of God today dwell in Esau's city and learn his ways.

And the earth was filled with violence: just like Cain was violent. Is the earth full of violence today? Yes. The end of all flesh is come before me; behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Luke traces Christ's line all the way back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” There it is written plainly. Adam was the son of God, and that line, Seth's line, were the sons of God of Genesis 6.

Abel was one of them, but Cain killed him. Then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel, and the line of the sons of God continued through him.

So “the sons of God saw the daughters of men” is Seth's line looking upon Cain's daughters. What followed is why “it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth.” The sons of God started to behave like Cain and his daughters, and God said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth”: destroy everything and start over. “The earth also was corrupt before God,” because the sons of God mingled with Cain's children; Cain gained dominion, “and the earth was filled with violence,” just as Cain was violent.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God in that time who were doing wickedness with Cain's daughters, Noah did not. There is always that light shining in the darkness all throughout time.

What does perfect mean, and what does it mean to walk with God? God told Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says Noah walked with God, it does not mean he went on long walks and talks on the beach with God. It means he walked in his ways.

Righteous, perfect and just all mean keeping God's commandments. The commandments that Seth kept, Noah was keeping also, while all flesh around him corrupted its way upon the earth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
God said of Abraham, “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” That is what it means to walk before God and be perfect.

Abraham kept the laws, statutes and commandments just as Noah did. “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God”: he kept the commandments that Seth kept, and that is why he found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the rest of the earth was corrupt and filled with violence.

So the law was not new at Sinai. Noah kept it, Abraham kept it, and those who keep it are the ones God preserves when “The end of all flesh is come before me.”

precepts.text: The sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair, and took them wives of all which they chose. The wickedness in verse 5 is that mixing the Most High said not to do; it grieved him at his heart, and judgment followed the chosen line into Egypt.
precepts.point: Why did God allow it? Because the sons of God broke God's law before it.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ spoke to Abram, before his name was changed to Abraham: “Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years.” That seed runs through Isaac, not through Abraham’s other children; Paul expounds that in Romans 9. The other nations are not God’s chosen people. And this first affliction is not America; it is ancient Egypt, where Jacob and the souls with him walked in.

So why did God bring that judgment on us? What did the sons of God do? They mixed with the daughters of men. Genesis 6: “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” The sons of God are the chosen line that came out of Seth, who replaced Abel after Cain killed him.

“There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” Then: “God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” The wickedness of verse 5 is that very thing: the sons of God taking the daughters of men to themselves, when the Most High had said not to do it.

“And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.” Now we know why the Most High told Abraham that his seed would surely end up serving in Egypt four hundred years. As the sons of God we broke his laws, and he brought forth judgment, rightfully so.

Therefore the world knoweth us not: they call us Negroes and refuse to believe these are the people of the book, because it knew him not; to this day they refuse to say Christ was a black man of the tribe of Judah.
precepts.point: After the Most High sent the flood, those same spirits came right back through the three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Genesis 5 traces the lineage from Adam down to Noah, who “begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Then Genesis 6 says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair.” The sons of God are that lineage just named; the daughters of men are the daughters of the other nations that were created. These are not literal angels. The chapter before gives the understanding, and the scriptures that follow prove who the sons of God are.

John writes it in the New Testament: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.” That is what God calls us. Brothers, you are walking gods, whoever gets upset about it, the apologists included.

“therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” The world looks at our people, calls us Negroes, and refuses to believe these could be the people of the book, the sons of God. And it knew him not: to this day they refuse to say Christ was a black man. They put the image of Cesare Borgia in every church, comic book and piece of media, while the Bible says he is black, of the tribe of Judah.

So when Genesis 6 speaks of “the sons of God” going in to the daughters of men, it is speaking of the same people John calls the sons of God: Adam’s line, our forefathers.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
“the sons of God saw the daughters of men” in Genesis 6 is about men, not spirits; God says “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh.” Psalms 82:6 shows who these sons of God are and what God calls them: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

We are gods, and we are children of the Most High. That is why the sons of God in Genesis 6 are called by that name: they carried that DNA, made in the image of God.

It is also why their sin was so serious. Back in Genesis 6:4, “There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men.” The sons of God, the children of the Most High, took wives of the other nations, which was forbidden. The children born to them “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and “God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” So the Most High brought destruction, and later we had to pay for what we did as the sons of God; he told Abraham his seed would be afflicted in a land not theirs for four hundred years.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
The sons of God in Genesis 6 are Adam’s line, the lineage traced in Genesis 5. Did that name change later, after the flood and after Egypt? No. Deuteronomy 14:1, spoken after the Exodus, says to Israel: “Ye are the children of the Lord your God.”

We are the children of the Lord our God because we are the sons of God. The same people carried the same title from Adam through Noah, through the fathers, out of Egypt, and into the law.

This matters for reading Genesis 6 rightly. The sons of God who went in to the daughters of men were not angels coming down from the sky; they were men of that same chosen line, God’s own children, who mixed with the other nations when it was forbidden. That sin brought the flood, and later the affliction of our people. The scriptures do not change the name: from Genesis, to Deuteronomy, to the prophets, to the New Testament, it is our people who are called the children and the sons of God.

precepts.why:
The title “sons of God” runs through the whole book. After Deuteronomy called Israel “the children of the Lord your God,” did anything change in the prophets? No. Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people.” That place is where our people are today: America and the diaspora, Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Europe. Everywhere we were told we are not God’s people. “there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

God calls us the sons of the living God. That is who we are. So the sons of God of Genesis 6 are the same nation the prophet speaks of: the children of Israel, scattered and counted as nothing, yet still his sons. The world does not know us, but God does, and in the very place where we were called not his people, he will call us his sons again.

The sons of the Titans and the high giants are those giants, the men of renown of Genesis 6, the offspring of the sons of God.

That is where Esau gets his Titan movies, and his Greek mythology of Hercules and the half-gods. He always mixes some lies in with the truth. He tells those stories because he looks at us as gods: because of our DNA, our physical prowess, our melanin. We are the sons of God, demigods on the earth, and that is why when our people are put into sports or anything physical, we dominate. Everybody wants our rhythm, but nobody wants our blues.

So the Titans of the Greek stories are not fallen angels or gods of another people. They are a twisted memory of the mighty men born when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Baruch says the same thing as Genesis 6: “There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.” Those giants were the offspring of the sons of God, the mighty men of renown, and they were expert in war as well.

“Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them.” God did not choose them; they were wicked. “But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.” How were they destroyed? The flood. God saw that “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually,” and he wiped it out.

But those same spirits came right back, by way of the three sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun. Jude speaks of “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation,” the same words, “of old,” that Genesis 6 uses of the men of renown. The same kind of wickedness is still here, reserved “unto the judgment of the great day,” which has not yet come.

So the giants are not a fantasy of fallen angels, the Nephilim Esau talks about. They were men, the offspring of the sons of God, who had no wisdom, and whose spirit lives on until the judgment.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
All of this was happening in the city called Enoch, named after Cain's son. Genesis says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” In Christianity they say the sons of God are angels coming down. John shows who the sons of God are: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”.

The sons of God is not talking about angels. It is talking about men, our people. Before we were called Israelites, we were called the sons of God.

Genesis 6 proves it: “And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh”. God is angry with man, the sons of God, who are flesh, not angels. It is hard to see how Christian scholars can read that and say angels.

So when the sons of God took them wives of all which they chose, it is talking about interracial marriage: we started marrying the women of other nations. It still happens, a brother bringing in a white woman and claiming she is of the tribe of Gad, when everybody knows she is an Edomite.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Everybody is waiting for our manifestation, for us to be called the sons of God. That is the same name Genesis 6 gives, which settles who the sons of God were: men of our people, not angels.

With that understanding, Genesis 6 reads plainly. It says that “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” That spark from God that we had produced renowned and powerful men on the earth, and they were battling the giants.

But we were not righteous; we had already started breaking God's laws inside that city. “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” Think of the great cities today, like New York City: murder, wicked music, buying and selling, stealing. It is the same thing going on now that was going on then, down to a married man looking over at other nations' women.

“The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.” God told Noah, “the earth is filled with violence through them”, and that “them” goes back to Cain's seed. What we read in Genesis 4 about Cain's children affected all people on the earth. So God said, “Make thee an ark of gopher wood”. The sons of God were meant to be manifest, but by mixing with Cain's world they were corrupted with it.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
“And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.” The angels here are the sons of God from the beginning of the Bible: Seth's line, Adam's chosen, righteous line of children.

Jude 7 shows what they did: “Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh”. In like manner means the angels of verse 6 did the same thing the Sodomites did: gave themselves over to fornication. The strange flesh is the sons of God stepping outside their own line and dealing with Cain's lineage, the daughters of men.

Genesis 6 is that fornication: “That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Then, “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” God cut their lifespan short because of it. The sons of God went into fornication, and that is how they fell from their first estate.

They were reserved in chains under darkness. Like the prophets and seers whose eyes were covered, they were reserved from the beginning to reject Christ, the black Messiah. Their fathers were murderers, and the same murderers came back in their children.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Psalm 82 opens: “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” We are the mighty and we are the gods. Then: “How long will ye judge unjustly”? What did we do? Genesis 6:1 tells it: “And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them”. Nations were beginning to form on the earth. Then verse 2 speaks of “the sons of God”.

Who are the sons of God? Exodus 4:22: “And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”. Now we know who the sons of God are. It is not talking about angels; it is talking about us, before we were called Israel. Before the flood, we were called the sons of God.

“That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” We started taking wives of the other nations, and there were laws on that. Deuteronomy 7:3-4: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them”, “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Joshua 23:13 warns that such nations “shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes”. These nations, you marry them, and they are snares and traps unto you. Black women who said the white man is better than the black man were put to death by the men they chose. Sherrone Moore already had a white woman at home, but that was not good enough; he needed a young white woman, and he lost everything for a white coontang. That's a snare and a trap right there. Halle Berry has to pay $8,000 a month to that Edomite, and when she pays him, he says thank you, nigger, and walks away. You can't make this stuff up. Tobit 4:12 says to “take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”, for “our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children”.

That was how we judged unjustly and accepted the persons of the wicked. God's son, his firstborn, broke the law he already had, and the Lord said, “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” He cut down our lifespan.

precepts.text: We are called the sons of God.
precepts.point: Their children turned into giants and wickedness, and man's days were cut to 120 years.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
After Exodus 4:22, 1 John 3:1 confirms it: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”. We who? We Israelites. The sons of God of Genesis 6 are not angels; they are us.

So Genesis 6 is about our fathers: “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” Our sons became famous men. “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” The man God was angry with was the sons of God. Once we broke the laws we already had and went in unto the daughters of men, our kids turned into the devil and started acting like the devil on the planet. That is why God had to bring the flood.

Psalm 82:6-7 says of us: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High. But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” The flood came and we all died, and we came back through Noah's son Shem. And we still have not learned our lesson. Today the same snares catch our men and women who leave their own people for other nations, and it costs them everything.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All creation is waiting for the sons of God, Israel, to be revealed. The sons of God fell in Genesis 6 by judging unjustly, but the plan still stands.

Psalm 82:8: “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.” Psalm 2:8 says to Christ: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” And we are joint heirs: Romans 8:17, “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”. What Christ gets, he gives to us. Revelation 2:26-27: “to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”, “even as I received of my Father.”

Christ has made us “kings and priests” (Revelation 1:6), and Paul says, “Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” The saints are the children of Israel, as Psalm 148:14 says. “Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” The angels we will judge are not Michael or Gabriel; they are each other, the twelve tribes, as Christ promised the twelve would sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

That is the manifestation creation is waiting for. We may look like nobody now, but in time we will rule the nations with Christ. All we have to do is endure to the end.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Noah's ark was built the same way. “A window shalt thou make to the ark”: there is that window again, like the narrow windows of the temple. “and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof”: the door is in the side of the boat. “with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.” A lower level, a second level and a third.

The ark had three levels, the same as the temple. It is basically a floating temple. God gave Noah the same pattern he gave Solomon, and both follow the way the heavens are built.

Temple, ark and heavens all show the same three stories, and that is how Paul could speak of being caught up to the third heaven. Paradise is the third story, and the Father dwells above all of it.

precepts.text: Moses reiterated to the sons of God the law against taking wives of the other nations.
precepts.point: The law against marrying into the other nations began here in Genesis. It was already known, and Moses had to reiterate that same law to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations; they were not the direct descendants of Adam. The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in chapter 5. That is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men, and the sons of God “took them wives of all which they chose.”

The law against marrying into the other nations began right here in Genesis. It was already known. Moses had to reiterate that same law to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” What the sons of God did in Genesis 6 is exactly what Moses forbade.

precepts.text: The angels left their first estate as sons of God, and the Most High reserved them unto judgment.
precepts.point: The angels which kept not their first estate are these same men of Genesis 6:4; they came from the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God. Another word for angel is messenger.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
The giants in the earth came from the sons of God intermingling with the other nations. The children born to them “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.”

Jude speaks of “the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation”. Those angels are these same men of Genesis 6:4. Another word for angel is messenger. They came from the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God; when they came in unto the daughters of men they left that estate. For it the Most High “hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.”

precepts.text: Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant unto the earth when the flood came.
precepts.point: Without Noah none of us would be here; Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
Genesis says Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord, that he “was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Ecclesiasticus says the same of him: “Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; therefore was he left as a remnant unto the earth, when the flood came.”

Without Noah none of us would be here. He was the remnant left unto the earth, and his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood. “An everlasting covenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.”

precepts.text: Faith is the evidence of things not seen; with Noah the thing not seen was rain.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
“Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.” Noah did it by faith. “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”

With Noah the thing not seen was rain. Up to that time rain had never been seen, and it takes faith to build an ark for a thing that has never happened. That is the faith we must have to prepare our households for when Christ comes back.

precepts.text: By faith Noah, warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear and prepared an ark to the saving of his house.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
Paul says “without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.” Noah pleased the Most High because he did all that was commanded him by faith.

“By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house”. The thing not seen as yet was rain; it had never happened, and he built anyway. By that ark “he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.”

As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back, and that takes the same faith. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

precepts.text: The longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah while the ark was preparing, and eight souls were saved by water.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
While the ark was preparing, Noah was not silent. He was a preacher of righteousness telling his people to repent, and “the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing”. The Most High waited for them to repent, and they were disobedient.

In the end “few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.” Understand that: the ones that were actually in the water died. The eight were saved in the ark while the water destroyed everyone else, so this is not talking about getting baptized.

precepts.text: Noah was the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
The Most High “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”. Noah was the eighth person, the eight souls of 1 Peter 3:20, and he was a preacher of righteousness.

So while he did all that God commanded him and built the ark, he was also preaching, telling his people to repent, while the longsuffering of the Most High waited for them. They did not, and the flood came upon the world of the ungodly.

precepts.text: As the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.
precepts.point: As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back; that takes the same faith. In the days of Noah they were eating, drinking, and marrying until Noah entered the ark and there was no more chance to repent; so shall the coming of the Son of man be. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
Christ puts Noah’s day next to his own return: “But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” In the days before the flood “they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark”. Once Noah entered the ark there was no more chance to repent; they “knew not until the flood came, and took them all away”.

And “so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” That is why Noah doing all that God commanded him matters to us. As Noah prepared the ark to the saving of his house, we must prepare our households for when Christ comes back, with the same faith he had. We have to put on the spirit of Noah.

precepts.text: The Most High set man's days at a hundred and twenty years.
precepts.point: A quarrel then arose between the men of Israel and the men of Judah over who had the right to bring the king back. Judah claimed the king was near of kin to them, being of the tribe of Judah, while Israel claimed ten parts in the king and more right in David, and the words of Judah were fiercer than the words of Israel. This was the tribe strife that would later split the northern and southern kingdoms, though they were all Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” The Most High set man’s days at a hundred and twenty years.

Barzillai the Gileadite was “a very aged man, even fourscore years old”. At eighty he asked, “How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?” He could no longer taste what he ate or drank, nor hear “the voice of singing men and singing women”. He would go only a little way over Jordan, and asked to turn back, “that I may die in mine own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother.”

Man’s days were set at a hundred and twenty years, yet at fourscore Barzillai was already very aged and ready to die.

precepts.text: When the wickedness of man was great and every imagination of his heart only evil, the Most High grieved and purposed to destroy man from the face of the earth; a repeated pattern of evil brings his judgment.
precepts.point: The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
The Most High “saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” It grieved him at his heart, and he said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth.”

That is the pattern behind the fall of Jerusalem. Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the Lord his God, humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet, stiffened his neck and hardened his heart. The chief of the priests and the people transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen and polluted the house of the Lord.

A repeated pattern of evil brings his judgment. The Most High sent his messengers, rising up betimes, because he had compassion; but they mocked the messengers, despised his words and misused his prophets, “until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.” As in the days before the flood, when the wickedness is great and continual, destruction comes.

precepts.text: God saw the wickedness of man was great, and every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually; this is how we differ from the world, keeping the Commandments.
precepts.point: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why:
Before Sodom, he looked down in the days of Noah: “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” When he looked, he saw wickedness, and every imagination of the thoughts of man's heart only evil continually.

This is how we differ from the world: keeping the Commandments. God looks down to see if there are any that understand and seek him, and the ones keeping his Commandments are the ones he finds.

precepts.text: It repented the Most High that he had made man, and it grieved him at his heart.
precepts.point: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why: “And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.” When the Most High looked down and saw the wickedness of man great in the earth, it repented him that he had made man and grieved him at his heart. God looking down upon the children of men to see if any understand is not idle; what he sees moves him.

precepts.text: The Most High said he would destroy man from the face of the earth.
precepts.point: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why: “And the Lord said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them.” Having looked down and found the wickedness great, the Most High said he would destroy man from the face of the earth. That is the judgment that follows when he looks and finds none that understand or seek him.

precepts.text: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Most High; he was a just man, perfect in his generation, and walked with God.
precepts.point: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why: “But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” When God looked down from heaven upon the children of men to see if any did understand and seek him, he found Noah, a just man, perfect in his generation, who walked with God. The whole earth was only evil continually, and one man found grace. That is how we differ from the world: keeping the Commandments and walking with God, so that when he looks down he finds us.

precepts.text: My spirit shall not always strive with man; his days shall be a hundred and twenty years, as He constantly cuts our days short.
precepts.point: The days of our years are threescore years and ten; a score is twenty, so three score and ten is seventy. At seventy you must give up the ghost, for the Lord's spirit will not always be striving with you.

note.label: Psalm 90: Teach Us to Number Our Days

precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” A score is twenty, so threescore and ten is seventy. At seventy you must give up the ghost, for the Lord's spirit will not always be striving with you.

That goes back to the flood: “And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” His spirit shall not always strive with man, and man's days were set at a hundred and twenty years. He constantly cuts our days short, from a hundred and twenty down to seventy or eighty.

We are consumed by his anger, and he has set our iniquities before him, our secret sins in the light of his countenance. That is how the Lord can judge you; we don't get away. In the regeneration they shall live again, and then the works of the righteous and the works of the wicked shall be declared. Our years are spent as a tale that is told.
